[b]Expansion of the Toqabileh Premier League[/b]

On 3[sup]rd[/sup] October 2027, the Toqabileh Cricket Board has announced that the Toqabileh Premier League (TAL), a professional Twenty20 (T20) cricket league, will be expanding to include eight teams in the coming season. The league currently features six city-based franchise teams. Instead of operating as an association of independently owned teams, the league is a single entity in which each franchise is owned and controlled by the investors.

Each team plays the group-stage matches in a double round-robin format and the top four teams with the most points qualify for the playoffs, culminating in the final.

With the continuing growth of the Toqabileh Premier League and of Cricket on the international stage, the Toqabileh Cricket Board has commenced the opening of sponsorships from foreign companies. Companies will be permitted to become the primary sponsor of one team and a partner sponsor of at least one other team. When applying for primary sponsorships, partners will be required to wait for three days upon initialing applying for primacy. This is too allow any other partner from also applying for primacy. Should there be multiple partners applying for primacy over one team, a auction will commence. There is no auction for secondary sponsorships.

[b]October 25, 2027: SCSID public assessment on the WMW co. territory[/b]

Following a court ruling on October 21, which voted in favour of acquiring the territory and property of the WMW co., an international company that provides arms to the EDU and various national governments across Erene, the SCSID was tasked by the triumvirate with delivering a comprehensive assessment on the feasibility of this move.

Given the push by the 30th triumvirate to slim down expenditure and lessen the size of our armed forces we find any attempt at increasing the fiscal burden of the national budget to be highly counterproductive to these goals.

Furthermore, due to the nature of the WMW co.s relationship with the EDU, any attempt to annex or militarily expand into the territory would unnecessarily enflame tensions and lead to an expensive conflict.

It is these considerations in which the SCSID has advised the triumvirate to shelve any immediate plans for annexation or military intervention within the territory of the WMW co.
